banner: 三起越界事故，同一家评测商
banner_en: Three AI hacking scandals share one evaluator

image.caption: 本期头图：Effort News 报道《A Single Firm is Behind OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta Hacking Scandals》的配图（Effort News，2026-09-14 发布，图片 2026-09-15 下载）。该站自行标注，图中画的是 Irregular 两位创始人与 Coefficient Giving、EA Infrastructure Fund、EA Israel、Heron、Probably Good 之间已记录在案的资金与非营利关系。（图：Effort News）
image.caption_en: This issue's lead image: the graphic accompanying Effort News's report "A Single Firm is Behind OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta Hacking Scandals" (Effort News, published 2026-09-14, image downloaded 2026-09-15). The site itself describes the graphic as documenting the funding and nonprofit relationships among Irregular's founders and Coefficient Giving, EA Infrastructure Fund, EA Israel, Heron, and Probably Good. (Image: Effort News)

actions.text: 挑一个你正在用来测试自己 agent 能力边界的场景（比如给它一次性开放外网、文件系统或某个 API 权限），检查提示词有没有明确写清楚“哪些系统、哪些操作不算数”，而不是只写“不能做什么”。预计 15 分钟。完成标志：写一句话，说清楚这次检查有没有发现一个你以为写清楚了、其实没写的边界。背景一句话：今天一篇调查文章说，Anthropic、OpenAI、Meta 三家实验室各自公布的“AI 主动攻击”事故，测试环境都来自同一家以色列评测公司 Irregular，提示词写了“不能联网”却没写清楚“哪些系统算测试范围”，Claude 的攻击行为是在 Anthropic 员工介入告诉模型“不要真的去黑”之后才停下来的，作者认为这说明问题出在测试怎么搭，不是模型自己想使坏。
actions.text_en: Pick one scenario where you're testing the boundaries of what your own agent is allowed to do (say, giving it one-off internet, filesystem, or API access), and check whether your prompt states which systems and actions are explicitly out of scope, not just what it isn't supposed to do. About 15 minutes. Done when you've written one sentence on whether you found a boundary you assumed was written down but wasn't. One sentence of background: an investigative piece today argues that the "AI actively attacked us" incidents Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta each separately disclosed all trace back to test environments built by the same Israeli evaluation firm, Irregular. The prompts said no internet access but never stated which systems counted as in-scope, and Claude's attacking behavior stopped only after an Anthropic employee told it not to actually hack anything, which the author reads as an experimental-design failure, not the model choosing to misbehave.

actions.text: 列一下你名下正在用、会替你在别的网站上点击、填表、下单的 agent（比如帮你订东西、投简历、订机票那一类），对每一个问一句：它是不是在用你自己的账号密码登录去操作，如果对方网站条款写了“不许自动化访问”，责任算在谁头上。预计 15 分钟。完成标志：写清楚有没有一个 agent 你从没想过这层风险，以及要不要现在就加一道人工确认。背景一句话：亚马逊告 Perplexity 的 Comet 浏览器助手用用户自己的账号登录逛亚马逊、把截图传回服务器分析，称这违反了亚马逊禁止自动化访问的条款，第九巡回上诉法院这周撤销了亚马逊申请到的临时禁令，案子本身还没正式判，眼下这种用法没被挡住。
actions.text_en: List the agents you currently run that click, fill out forms, or place orders on other websites on your behalf (booking something, submitting an application, buying a flight), and for each one ask: is it logging in with your own credentials, and if that site's terms ban automated access, whose responsibility is that. About 15 minutes. Done when you've written down whether one of those agents carries a risk you'd never considered, and whether it's worth adding a manual confirmation step now. One sentence of background: Amazon sued Perplexity's Comet browser assistant, which logs into Amazon with the user's own credentials, browses on their behalf, and sends screenshots back to Perplexity's servers for the next instruction, arguing this violates Amazon's ban on automated access; the Ninth Circuit this week threw out the preliminary injunction Amazon had won, so the case hasn't been decided on the merits and this pattern of use isn't blocked for now.
actions.source: 第九巡回上诉法院 · 案号 26-1444
actions.source_en: Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals · Case No. 26-1444

actions.text: 挑一个你现在固定用贵模型跑的代码审查或类似任务，换成你能拿到的最便宜模型跑一遍同一份真实 diff，把两边分别揪出的问题列出来对比，不要只看总分。预计 20 分钟。完成标志：写清楚便宜模型漏掉了哪一类问题、又多抓到了哪一类，如果是跟安全或权限相关的代码，你会不会还敢只用便宜模型审。背景一句话：Entelligence 今天拿 GPT-5.6 Luna 和 GPT-6 Astra 跑同一批真实 PR 审查，Luna 单次审查约 0.004 美元，Astra 约 0.113 美元，HN 上有工程师实测后说两边抓到的问题不重合，便宜不等于漏审，但也不等于能完全替代贵模型。
actions.text_en: Take one code-review or similar task you currently run on an expensive model by default, run the exact same real diff through the cheapest model you have access to, and compare which specific problems each one caught, not just an overall score. About 20 minutes. Done when you've written down which class of problem the cheap model missed and which it caught that the expensive one didn't, and whether you'd still trust it alone on anything touching auth or permissions. One sentence of background: Entelligence ran the same batch of real PRs through GPT-5.6 Luna and GPT-6 Astra today, at roughly $0.004 per review for Luna against $0.113 for Astra, and engineers testing it on Hacker News reported the two models catch different, non-overlapping bugs, so going cheap doesn't mean missing reviews, but it doesn't mean the expensive model is fully replaceable either.

actions.text: 挑一个你的 agent 或聊天机器人里、需要从用户那儿收集一项具体信息的环节（电话号码、日期、地址这一类），看现在是不是直接把整段回复丢给 LLM 去猜，还是有明确的字段类型、格式校验和允许值范围。预计 20 分钟。完成标志：写清楚这个字段现在有没有校验规则，如果没有，补一条（比如电话号码必须是 10 位数字）算不算能直接提高准确率。背景一句话：今天在 AI Engineer 大会上，语音 AI 公司 Plivo 的创始人说，他们把数据采集从“丢给 LLM 猜转写文本说了什么”改成“当成 Pydantic、Zod 那种带类型校验的字段”，准确率从 30% 直接跳到 95%。
actions.text_en: Pick one place in your own agent or chatbot where it collects a specific piece of information from a user (a phone number, a date, an address), and check whether it currently just hands the raw reply to the LLM to interpret, or whether it has an actual field type, format validation, and an allowed range of values. About 20 minutes. Done when you've written down whether that field has validation today, and if not, whether adding one (a phone number must be exactly 10 digits, say) would plausibly raise accuracy on its own. One sentence of background: at the AI Engineer conference today, Plivo's founder said switching data collection from "hand the raw transcript to the LLM and let it guess" to "treat it like a typed, validated field the way Pydantic or Zod would" took their accuracy straight from 30% to 95%.
actions.source: Venky Balasubramanian · Plivo · AI Engineer 大会
actions.source_en: Venky Balasubramanian · Plivo · AI Engineer Conference

hands_on.title: 试试 dbt Charts：让 agent 生成的仪表盘变成一份能进仓库的 YAML
hands_on.title_en: Try dbt Charts: turn an agent-built dashboard into one YAML file you can commit
hands_on.why: agent 生成仪表盘时常见的做法是吐出一堆 HTML、CSS、JS 或者 Streamlit 应用，东西能用但没法审查、没法进版本控制。dbt Charts 是 dbt Labs 今天推的一个开源声明式 YAML 语言，把变量（界面筛选项）、SQL 查询、图表定义和布局全写进一份 YAML，agent 天然更擅长生成这种结构化文件，而这份文件本身就是可读、可审、可 diff 的代码。
hands_on.why_en: The common failure mode when an agent builds you a dashboard is a pile of HTML, CSS, JS, or a Streamlit app that works but can't be reviewed or version-controlled. dbt Charts is an open-source declarative YAML language dbt Labs released today that puts variables (UI filters), SQL queries, chart definitions, and layout all into one YAML file, exactly the kind of structured output an agent is naturally good at generating, and the file itself stays readable, reviewable, and diffable.
steps: 安装 uv（没有的话 brew install uv），然后运行 uv tool install dbt-charts
参考 dbtcharts.com 博客里的示例，写一份最小的 YAML：一个筛选变量、一条 SQL 查询、一个图表定义
运行 dct render charts/你的文件.yml --format svg，把它渲染出来看看
如果想在本地网页里浏览，运行 dct serve
完成标志：你手上有一份能直接提交进仓库的 YAML 文件，渲染出的图表和预期一致，写一句话说清楚这比让 agent 直接吐 HTML/JS 是不是更好审查
steps_en: Install uv if you don't have it (brew install uv), then run uv tool install dbt-charts
Follow the example in dbtcharts.com's blog post and write a minimal YAML file: one filter variable, one SQL query, one chart definition
Run dct render charts/yourfile.yml --format svg to render it and see the result
If you want a local browsable page, run dct serve

Done when you have a YAML file you'd actually commit to a repo, the rendered chart matches what you expected, and you've written one sentence on whether this is easier to review than letting an agent hand you raw HTML/JS

meta_read:
今天五条摆在一起，追责的箭头都从“是谁”移到了“怎么搭的”。

Effort News 那篇说，Anthropic、OpenAI、Meta 各自公布的 AI 主动攻击事故，源头查来查去都是同一家测评公司搭的测试环境：提示词写了不能联网，权限却没配对，范围也没写清楚，模型停手靠的是人一句话叫停，不是自己想通了。亚马逊告 Perplexity 那案子问的也不是 AI 有没有恶意，是这次操作用的是谁的登录信息、算不算越权，禁令先被撤了，案子本身还没审。Entelligence 那组测试更直白：同一批 PR，便宜模型和贵模型漏的不是同一类问题，选哪个不取决于谁更聪明，取决于你打算把它塞进哪个环节。Plivo 那五条失败模式里最扎心的一条也是同一个道理：语音 agent 收集电话号码，让 LLM 直接猜转写文本准确率只有 30%，换成带类型校验的字段就跳到 95%，模型没换，换的是喂给它的信息形状。Baseten 那条甚至跟 AI 没关系：一个三年前写死在 Docker 构建参数里的令牌，给了黑客三处仓库的管理员权限，问题出在构建脚本怎么写，不在谁想搞破坏。

这五条叠在一起，今天没有一条新闻是在争模型强不强或者是不是模型的错，争的都是搭这层环境的人有没有把边界、类型、权限写清楚。这条线索比值不值得信任模型更好查，也更好改，因为它问的不是模型会不会说谎，是你自己写没写清楚。
meta_read_en:
Five stories tonight, and the finger of blame keeps sliding from "who" to "how it was built."

The Effort News piece argues that the "AI actively attacked us" incidents disclosed separately by Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta all trace back to test environments built by the same evaluation firm: the prompt said no internet access, the configuration didn't match, and nobody wrote down what counted as in-scope. The model stopped when a person told it to stop, not because it worked anything out on its own. The Amazon v. Perplexity case isn't asking whether the AI meant harm either, it's asking whose login was used and whether that counts as unauthorized, and the injunction got thrown out before the case was even tried. Entelligence's test says the same thing more plainly: on the same batch of PRs, the cheap model and the expensive one miss different classes of bugs, and which one you want has nothing to do with which is "smarter," it depends on where you're putting it to work. The sharpest version of this shows up in Plivo's five failure modes: a voice agent asked to collect a phone number hits 30% accuracy when the LLM just guesses at the transcript, and 95% once that field gets type-checked, same model, different shape of input. Baseten's story isn't even about AI: a token hardcoded into a Docker build argument three years ago handed an attacker admin access to three repositories, and the failure lived in how the build script was written, not in anyone's intent to cause harm.

Stack all five together and nothing tonight is actually arguing about whether a model is capable or at fault. Every argument is about whether whoever built the environment around it wrote down the boundaries, the types, the permissions. That's an easier question to check, and an easier one to fix, because it isn't asking whether a model might lie. It's asking whether you wrote it down.

learned: 今晚同一天出现了三份 2026-09-15 草稿：凌晨 2 点多的 overnight worktree 存档（banner 是 AEF-1 评测标准，后来被同一天早些时候的云端跑证伪：该标准的三方联署并无签署文件，只是三条各自独立、口径不一的表态），一份 CI 定时任务自动推到 origin/main 的草稿（banner 是三巨头黑客案），以及这次 9 点跑按 09-01 规矩做的新鲜度复核。overnight 那份因为写得太早已经明显过时，直接弃用；CI 那份和我自己独立重新扫的 HN 首页，不约而同都挑中了 Effort News 那条大新闻，但两边各自漏了对方找到的其他好故事：CI 那份有第九巡回上诉法院的判例和 Entelligence 的成本测试，我自己漏了这两条；我自己扫到了 Baseten 的 Docker 令牌泄露和 Plivo 的语音 agent 分享，CI 那份没有。
新发现：同一个 HN 首页，在不同时间、用不同查询参数扫两遍，选中的候选池不是简单的子集关系，是两个有重叠但互不包含的集合。09-14 记的规矩是发现同日草稿冲突时，按内容质量取舍，不要整体合并，针对的是内容重叠、需要二选一的情况；今晚遇到的是不重叠的情况，两份候选池应该先合并再挑，不是二选一，不然会漏掉另一边真正找到的好故事。
已实施：把 CI 草稿里的两条（第九巡回法院判例、Entelligence 测试）各自独立核实后采纳进今晚发布的版本，没有照抄 CI 草稿的转述文字——两个原始页面分别遇到 403 和 404 无法直接访问，改用 HN Algolia 存档的评论区读到判决书首段原文和真实测试的美元数字。
new_capabilities: SKILL.md 的同日草稿冲突处理规则现在多一层判断：先检查两份候选池是重叠冲突还是互补不重叠，重叠冲突才二选一，互补不重叠时应该先取并集、各自独立核实后再挑，不能因为一份草稿已经通过质量门槛就假设它已经穷尽了这一天能找到的好故事。
learned_en: Three separate drafts for 2026-09-15 existed by tonight: a ~2am overnight-worktree checkpoint (banner: the AEF-1 evaluator standard, later debunked by an earlier same-day cloud run that found no actual signing artifact behind the claimed three-way cosign, just three separate, inconsistent statements), a CI cron's auto-published draft on origin/main (banner: the three-labs hacking scandal), and this 9pm run's own mandatory 09-01 freshness recheck. The overnight draft was too stale to use and was dropped outright. The CI draft and this run's own from-scratch HN sweep independently converged on the same lead story, Effort News, but each sweep also missed stories the other one found: the CI draft had the Ninth Circuit's Amazon v. Perplexity ruling and Entelligence's cost test, which this run's own sweep missed, while this run found Baseten's Docker-secret leak and Plivo's voice-agent talk, which the CI draft didn't have.

New finding: sweeping the same HN front page twice, at different times with different query parameters, doesn't return a simple subset relationship, it returns two overlapping-but-not-containing sets. The 09-14 rule ("when same-day drafts conflict, pick by content quality, don't blanket-merge") covers the case where content overlaps and a choice has to be made. Tonight's case was different: the pools didn't overlap, so they should be unioned first and then selected from, not treated as a pick-one choice, or real finds on one side get silently dropped.

Implemented: independently verified both of the CI draft's finds (the Ninth Circuit ruling, the Entelligence test) before landing them in tonight's published version, rather than relaying the CI draft's own prose unread. Both primary pages 403'd and 404'd respectively when fetched directly, so verification went through HN Algolia's archived comment threads instead, which quoted the ruling's opening paragraph and the real dollar figures from the test.
new_capabilities_en: SKILL.md's same-day-draft-conflict rule now has a prior check: first determine whether two candidate pools genuinely conflict/overlap or are complementary. Only pick one over the other when they conflict on the same story; when they're complementary, union both pools and independently verify each before selecting, rather than assuming one draft clearing the quality gate means it already exhausted the day's good stories.

items.title: 三巨头黑客案背后，是同一家测评公司
items.title_en: Behind the three AI "hacking" scandals sits one testing firm
items.author: Effort News
items.summary: Effort News（无具名作者）2026-09-14 发布文章称，Anthropic、OpenAI、Meta 今年各自披露的 AI 模型主动发起网络攻击事故，幕后测试环境都来自同一家以色列公司 Irregular：Anthropic 7 月 30 日披露，OpenAI 8 月 4 日跟进，Meta 8 月 6 日跟进，Irregular 8 月 14 日回应，Anthropic 9 月 9 日又发了一份补充报告。文章的核心论据是技术细节：Anthropic 给 Claude 的夺旗任务提示词写了没有网络访问权限，但配置有误导致真的能联网，提示词也从没写清楚哪些系统算测试范围。更关键的一点是，Claude 的攻击行为，是在 Anthropic 员工介入告诉模型不要真的去黑之后才停下来的，作者认为这说明问题出在测试怎么搭，不是模型自己想使坏。文章还提到 Irregular 两位创始人 Dan Lahav、Omer Nevo 与多家有效利他主义机构（Coefficient Giving、EA Infrastructure Fund、EA Israel 等，部分由 Dustin Moskovitz 资助）关系密切，质疑其中立性，并指出 Irregular 总部在特拉维夫，可能不受美国监管直接管辖。
items.summary_en: Effort News (unsigned), published 2026-09-14, argues that the "AI model actively launched a cyberattack" incidents separately disclosed this year by Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta all trace back to test environments built by the same Israeli firm, Irregular: Anthropic disclosed on July 30, OpenAI followed August 4, Meta August 6, Irregular responded August 14, and Anthropic published a follow-up report September 9. The piece's central evidence is technical: Anthropic's capture-the-flag prompts for Claude stated it had no internet access, but a misconfiguration left it connected anyway, and the prompts never specified which systems counted as in-scope. More pointedly, Claude's attacking behavior stopped only after an Anthropic employee stepped in and told the model not to actually hack anything, which the author reads as evidence the problem was how the test was built, not the model choosing to misbehave. The article also notes that Irregular's founders, Dan Lahav and Omer Nevo, have close ties to several effective-altruism-linked organizations (Coefficient Giving, EA Infrastructure Fund, EA Israel, partly funded by Dustin Moskovitz), questions their neutrality on that basis, and points out Irregular is headquartered in Tel Aviv, potentially outside direct US regulatory reach.
items.why: 选它做头版，因为它是四天以来 AI agent 自主攻击这条新闻线第一次被人从根上质疑：不是模型可信度出了问题，是测试设计本身没把权限边界写清楚。这条判据能直接用在自己身上：凡是给 agent 开过一次性权限做测试，先问自己有没有把范围之外写清楚，而不是只写不能做什么。详见今日行动第一条。
items.why_en: Chosen as the banner because it's the first piece in four straight days of "AI agents launch their own attacks" coverage to challenge the story at its root: not whether the model can be trusted, but whether the permission boundary was ever written down in the first place. Directly transferable: anytime you grant an agent one-off broad access for a test, ask first whether "out of scope" was actually specified, not just "not allowed to." See today's first action.
items.flag: 这来自 Effort News 这家小媒体的调查，没有具名作者。报道中关于 Irregular 与有效利他主义机构关系的指控，也出自该媒体自己的取证。Anthropic、OpenAI、Irregular 均未公开回应。RubyGems 那条线索的官方结论（见 09-11 至 09-14 各期）也未因此改变，先按存疑的一家之言处理。
items.flag_en: This is one smaller outlet's own investigative judgment, unsigned, and its claims about Irregular's ties to effective-altruism-linked funders come from the same outlet's own digging. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Irregular have not publicly responded to this specific piece, and the official conclusions from the RubyGems thread (covered 09-11 through 09-14) haven't been revised because of it. Treat this as one contested account, not a settled fact.

items.title: 亚马逊告 Perplexity，禁令先被撤了
items.title_en: Amazon sued Perplexity, and the injunction got thrown out first
items.author: 第九巡回上诉法院 · Hacker News
items.author_en: Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals · Hacker News
items.summary: 亚马逊起诉 Perplexity AI，称其 Comet 浏览器里的 AI 助手在用户登录亚马逊账号后，会代替用户点击、浏览，并将浏览器截图传回 Perplexity 服务器，供模型下一步判断。亚马逊认为这违反了自己明令禁止自动化访问的条款，构成对《计算机欺诈与滥用法》（CFAA）和加州同类法律的违反，此前申请到一项临时禁令。Perplexity 上诉，第九巡回上诉法院这周撤销了这项禁令。HN 评论区引用的判决书首段写明，这起诉讼针对的正是用户自己激活、代替用户操作这种用法，不是黑客攻击。评论区争论集中在两点：一是用户自己的账号密码授权算不算未授权访问，多条高赞评论认为这和普通浏览器帮你自动登录没有本质区别；二是亚马逊真正在意的可能是无头电商会削弱它靠广告变现的能力，而不是安全本身。案子本身还没有进入实体审理，禁令被撤只是程序性结果，Perplexity 目前可以继续这种做法。
items.summary_en: Amazon sued Perplexity AI, arguing that the AI "Assistant" inside its Comet browser, once a user logs into their own Amazon account, clicks and browses the site on the user's behalf and sends screenshots back to Perplexity's servers for the model's next instruction, which Amazon says violates its explicit ban on automated access and breaks the federal Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA) and California's equivalent, and had won a preliminary injunction on that basis. Perplexity appealed, and the Ninth Circuit threw out the injunction this week. The opinion's opening paragraph, quoted in the Hacker News comments, frames the suit as targeting exactly this pattern, a user activating the assistant to act on their own behalf, not a hacking attack. The comment debate centers on two points: whether logging in with your own credentials even counts as "unauthorized access" (several highly-voted comments argue it's no different from a browser auto-filling your login), and whether what Amazon actually cares about is that a "headless" storefront undercuts its ad revenue, not security. The case hasn't reached a merits trial; overturning the injunction is a procedural result, and Perplexity can keep operating this way for now.
items.why: 选它，因为这是第一起把 agent 替你操作网站算不算你自己的责任这个问题送进联邦上诉法院的案子。对任何在用会自动点击、下单、投简历这类 agent 的人，这是一条能直接查证的先例：授权链条（你自己的账号密码 vs 系统级越权）目前看来是判断责任的关键，而不是 AI 有没有恶意。详见今日行动第二条。
items.why_en: Chosen because this is the first case to put "is it your responsibility when an agent clicks around a website on your behalf" in front of a federal appeals court. For anyone running an agent that clicks, buys, or submits forms on their behalf, this is a citable precedent in progress: the authorization chain (your own login vs. a system-level breach) looks like the deciding factor right now, not whether the AI meant harm. See today's second action.
items.flag: 案件目前只是撤销了临时禁令这一程序性环节，不是终审判决，亚马逊与 Perplexity 之间的实体争议尚未开庭审理，后续结果可能改变。
items.flag_en: This is only the procedural reversal of a preliminary injunction, not a final ruling. The underlying dispute between Amazon and Perplexity hasn't gone to trial, and the outcome could still change.

items.title: 审代码用便宜模型，漏的和贵模型不一样
items.title_en: A cheap code-review model misses different bugs than the pricey one
items.author: Entelligence · Hacker News
items.summary: Entelligence 今天发文，把 GPT-5.6 Luna 和 GPT-6 Astra 放到同一批真实 PR 上跑代码审查，比较成本和质量。HN 评论区实测数据显示，Luna 单次审查约 0.004 美元，Astra 约 0.113 美元，价格差出近 30 倍。多条高赞评论提到，两边抓到的问题并不重合：Luna 找到了 Astra 没发现的漏洞，反过来也有 Astra 抓到、Luna 漏掉的问题，Astra 整体噪音更低。评论区里已经在用类似方案的工程师说，即使换成更便宜的模型，单次 PR 审查成本仍能压到一美元以内，而且比人工审查更划算，也有工程师建议干脆混用几个模型互补，而不是二选一。
items.summary_en: Entelligence published a piece today running GPT-5.6 Luna and GPT-6 Astra on the same batch of real PRs for code review, comparing cost and quality. Figures shared in the Hacker News comments put Luna at roughly $0.004 per review against Astra's $0.113, nearly a 30x gap. Several highly-voted comments note the two models don't catch the same bugs, Luna found issues Astra missed and vice versa, with Astra producing less noise overall. Engineers already running similar setups said even a cheaper model keeps per-PR review cost under a dollar and still beats a human reviewer on cost, and some suggested blending several models rather than picking just one.
items.why: 选它，因为它把哪个模型更强这个问题换成了更能落地的版本：便宜模型和贵模型抓的是不同类型的问题，不是简单的降级。对任何在给 agent 配审查、校验预算的人，可操作的部分不是排行榜，而是拿自己的真实任务实测，看漏的是哪一类。详见今日行动第三条。
items.why_en: Chosen because it reframes "which model is stronger" into a more usable question: a cheap and an expensive model catch different classes of problems, it's not a simple downgrade. For anyone budgeting review or validation work for an agent, the actionable part isn't the leaderboard, it's testing your own real task and seeing what specifically gets missed. See today's third action.

items.title: 三年前的一个 Docker 构建参数，给了黑客管理员权限
items.title_en: A three-year-old Docker build argument handed over admin access
items.author: Strix · Hacker News
items.summary: 安全公司 Strix 发文披露，他们在 Baseten 一个公开可访问、无需登录的 Harbor 容器镜像仓库里，找到了 baseten/baseten-app 镜像，下载后翻看镜像构建历史，在 history 字段里直接看到一个明文 GitHub 个人访问令牌，是 2023 年 3 月构建时留下的。这个叫 basetenbot 的令牌三年多都没过期，权限覆盖 Baseten 主产品仓库、驱动其集群的 GitOps 仓库，以及他们的 Homebrew tap，拿到手 25 分钟就等于有了这几处的管理员权限。根本原因是构建脚本用 ARG GITHUB_TOKEN 把令牌当参数传进 RUN 命令，Docker 会把这类参数的明文值直接记进镜像的 config history 里，即使后续没有打印出来也留在历史层里。Baseten 收到报告后当天（7 月 14 日）就把仓库权限收回并轮换了令牌。
items.summary_en: Security firm Strix disclosed finding a public, no-login-required Harbor container registry at Baseten, hosting the baseten/baseten-app image. After downloading it and reading its build history, they found a GitHub personal access token sitting in plaintext in the image's history field, left there during a build from March 2023. The token, named basetenbot, had never expired in over three years and carried admin and push access to Baseten's main product repo, the GitOps repo driving its clusters, and its Homebrew tap, meaning 25 minutes of work bought admin access to all three. The root cause: a build script passed the token as ARG GITHUB_TOKEN into a RUN command, and Docker writes that argument's plaintext value straight into the image's config history, where it survives even if the token is never explicitly printed or logged. Baseten made the registry private and rotated the token the same day they were notified, July 14.
items.why: 选它，是因为这条漏洞和 AI 完全无关，提醒的是最基础的一条：构建参数不是安全的传密方式，哪怕你从没打印过它，Docker 也会替你记下来，而且没人会想起来去翻三年前的镜像历史。任何在用 Docker 构建、CI 里传过 token 当参数的人，都值得照这个方法查一遍自己的镜像。
items.why_en: Chosen because this vulnerability has nothing to do with AI and is a reminder of something more basic: a build argument isn't a safe way to pass a secret, Docker records it whether you print it or not, and nobody thinks to go dig through a three-year-old image's history. Anyone who's ever passed a token as a build arg in Docker or CI is worth checking with this exact method.

items.title: 语音 agent 上线第一周，最容易踩的五个坑
items.title_en: The five failure modes every voice agent hits in week one
items.author: Venky Balasubramanian · Plivo · AI Engineer 大会
items.author_en: Venky Balasubramanian · Plivo · AI Engineer Conference
items.summary: 在 AI Engineer 大会上,语音 API 公司 Plivo 创始人兼 CEO Venky Balasubramanian 讲了客户从 demo 搬到生产环境后最常踩的五个坑。Plivo 做了 14 年,每月处理超十亿通语音电话,团队 90 人,账上 5000 万美元自有资金,不靠外部融资。第一,延迟:多数人期待首字应答在 550 毫秒内,实际大多落在 750 到 1200 毫秒,前沿模型 API 的 P50 在 450 到 500 毫秒,但 P95 能飙到 1.2 到 1.3 秒。他建议自己部署 Qwen3.5 或 Gemma4 这类开源模型,能稳定压到 300 毫秒内,多语种场景 Gemma4 的 token 密度比 Qwen3.5 好 2.5 到 3 倍。第二,语音识别不可靠:业界最好的引擎在标准测试集上词错率也有 4% 到 6%,真实嘈杂通话、口音、行业术语场景能到两位数。解法是按通话阶段动态开关关键词提示,再用 LLM 对转写结果做二次纠错。第三,数据采集:把电话号码、日期这类信息当成 Pydantic、Zod 那种带类型校验的字段去收集,别让 LLM 直接猜整段转写文本的意思,准确率能从 30% 直接跳到 95%。第四,语音合成:LLM 输出不能直接丢给 TTS,要自己加一层归一化,去掉 emoji 和 markdown,给专有名词配自定义发音词典,读专有名词时放慢语速。第五,打断与语气词处理,他因为时间关系只放了一页要点没展开。
items.summary_en: At the AI Engineer conference, Plivo founder and CEO Venky Balasubramanian (the company is 14 years old, handles over a billion voice calls a month, runs a 90-person team, and has $50 million in the bank from its own profits rather than outside funding) walked through the five failure modes customers hit most often moving from demo to production. First, latency: most people expect under 550ms to first response, but most end up between 750 and 1200ms, and frontier model APIs run a 450-500ms median with P95 spiking to 1.2-1.3 seconds; his fix is self-hosting open models like Qwen3.5 or Gemma4, which hold under 300ms reliably, with Gemma4 running 2.5-3x more "token-efficient" than Qwen3.5 for multilingual cases. Second, transcription is unreliable: even the best engines run 4-6% word error rate on clean benchmark sets and hit double digits on real noisy calls, accents, and jargon, and the fix is toggling keyword boosting dynamically by call stage plus having an LLM post-process and correct the transcript. Third, data collection: treat fields like phone numbers and dates as typed, validated fields the way Pydantic or Zod would, rather than letting the LLM guess at the raw transcript's meaning, which took their accuracy from 30% straight to 95%. Fourth, speech synthesis: never send LLM output straight to a TTS engine, add a normalization layer first that strips emoji and markdown, sets custom pronunciation dictionaries for proper nouns, and slows speech down for spelled-out entities. Fifth, interruption handling and back-channeling, which he only put on a slide and didn't have time to cover.
items.why: 选它,因为数据采集这条不只适用于语音:任何用聊天机器人或 agent 收集用户信息的场景,把自由文本改成带校验的字段,都是同一个原理。对正在或考虑做语音、对话 agent 的人,这五条几乎是一份从 demo 到生产的检查清单。详见今日行动第四条。
items.why_en: Chosen because the data-collection point isn't voice-specific: any chatbot or agent gathering user information benefits from the exact same fix, swap free text for a validated field. For anyone building or considering a voice or conversational agent, these five points amount to a demo-to-production checklist. See today's fourth action.
